title: Picks of the Week Oct. 23
text:
Thursday, Oct. 23
"Waking up the Earth" poetry reading
4-5:30 p.m.; Westerly Library, 44 Broad St., Westerly
Margaret Gibson, former Connecticut Poet Laureate, Lisa Starr, former Rhode Island Poet Laureate, and Christie Max Williams, current Poet Laureate of Stonington, will be reading their own poems and selections of other poets. For more information, visit westerlylibrary.org or email brokencupgibson@gmail.com.
Olivia Charlotte, folk artist to perform
8 p.m.; The Knickerbocker Music Center, 35 Railroad Ave., Westerly
Free concert in the Tap Room. For more information, visit knickmusic.com.
Ghost Hunter Traci Boiselle
6 p.m.; Bill Memorial Library, 240 Monument St., Groton
Traci Boiselle, lead investigator and case manager for The Atlantic Paranormal Society will present "The Dead Do Speak." Boiselle, who has 16 years of experience in the field, will share basic theories of the paranormal, introduce attendees to the TAPS method of investigation, share experiences from some of her favorite local investigations and will answer questions. Registration is required. To register, visit tinyurl.com/34df9ctf or call 860-445-0392.
Oct. 23-Oct. 25
Westerly Library book sale
9 a.m.-6 p.m. on Thursday; 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m. on Friday; Saturday 9 a.m.-3:30 p.m. on Saturday, Westerly Library, 44 Broad St., Westerly
The Friends of Westerly Library and Wilcox Park will hold a book sale on the third floor of the library. Selections will include fiction, non-fiction, juvenile, cooking history, wellness, biography, mystery and travel. Saturday will feature a $10 bag sale.
Oct. 23-Nov. 2
"Witching Hour Social Club"
7:30 p.m.; Burbage Theatre Company, 59 Blackstone Ave., Pawtucket
A world premiere horror anthology play involving two estranged friends meeting in the woods on an autumn night for a high school storytelling club reunion. When it seems they’re the only club members coming, hopes for a big reunion dwindle. While waiting for friends to arrive, they listen to cassette tapes of old stories. But there’s more on the tapes than just old stories. Tickets are $16.50 to $35. For tickets and more information, visit burbagetheatre.org or call 401-484-0355.
Jack-o-Lantern Spectacular
6-10:30 p.m.; Roger Williams Zoo, 1000 Elmwood Ave., Providence
Thousands of carved pumpkins along a Halloween-inspired trail. Tickets are $19 to $23 and must be purchased online in advance. For more information and tickets, visit rwpzoo.org.
Oct. 23-26
"The Rocky Horror Show"
Various times; The Granite Theatre, 1 Granite St., Westerly
A musical directed by Patrick Berry, with music, lyrics and book by Richard O'Brien. For ages 17 and over. Tickets are $35 for adults, $32 for seniors, excluding taxes and fees. For more information, visit granitetheatre.org or call 401-596-2341.
What Lurks Beneath: A Halloween experience
Timed entries at 6, 6:30 and 7 p.m.; Mystic Seaport Museum, Greenmanville Ave., Mystic
Eerie indoor and outdoor spaces where ocean legends come alive will be featured. Tickets are $23-$30. For tickets and more information, visit msyticseaport.org.
"Pride and Prejudice" performance
Various; J-Studio, URI Fine Arts Center, 150 Upper College Road, Kingston
Director Kate Hamill's adaptation of the Jane Austen novel combines classical aspects of performance juxtaposed with contemporary text. Tickets are $20-$22. For tickets and more information, visit app.arts-people.
University of R.I. Guitar and Mandolin Festival and Luthier Expo
Various times; Various locations.
The University of Rhode Island will host a Guitar and Mandolin Festival with workshops, lectures and performances. For full schedule and tickets, visit urigmfest.org.
"Six the Musical"
Various: Providence Performing Arts Center, 220 Weybosset St., Providence
From Tudor Queens to Pop Icons, the six wives of Henry VIII take the microphone to remix five hundred years of historical heartbreak into a celebration of 21st century girl power. Tickets start at $54. For tickets and more information, visit ppacri.org or call 401-421-2787.
Fall Fest and Pumpkin Stroll
4-6 p.m.; Wilcox Park, 44 Broad St., Westerly
The Pumpkin Stroll will feature pumpkins decorated by members of the public, with prizes awarded. Free cider and doughnuts, children’s games and activities. Attendees are encouraged to come in costume for the costume parade at 5 p.m. Free pumpkins are available at the library on Friday, Oct. 17; contestants can also provide own pumpkins.
For more information, visit westerlylibrary.org, email reference@westerlylibrary.org or call 401-596-2877, ext. 306.
Eight to the Bar to perform
8 p.m.; The Knickerbocker Music Center, 35 Railroad Ave., Westerly
Swing, boogie woogie, rhythm and blues, soul and motown music. Tickets are $23. For tickets and more information, visit knickmusic.com.
Friday, Oct. 24
The Arts Café Mystic
7 p.m., La Grua Center, 32 Water St., Stonington
Poet Kimiko Hahn will share her poetry along with Poet Barbara Hill. Round Robin are the guest musicians. Tickets are available on the website, theartscafemystic.org or at the door at 6:30 p.m. Parking is both ample and free.
Oct. 24-26
FringePVD encore
Various; Wilbury Theatre Group, 475 Valley St., Providence
Wilbury Theatre Group presents the return of three shows from this July’s Providence Fringe Festival: “ Morality Play” by Lily Mathews, “The Farm” by Davis Alianiello and “When Cayden Came” by Charlotte Kinder. For tickets and more information, visit www.thewilburygroup.org or call 401-400-7100.
Oct. 24-Nov. 22
"Peter and the Starcatcher"
Various; Contemporary Theatre Company, 327 Main St., Wakefield
A world where Peter Pan is an orphan, Neverland is just an island, and one girl controls the stars. The family-friendly show reveals how Peter Pan got his name, how Captain Hook lost his hand, and how the two became nemeses. Tickets are $10 to $45. For tickets and more information, visit contemporarytheatercompany.com or call 401-218-0282.
Saturday, Oct. 25
The Irish Roots of Halloween
1-2 p.m.; Westerly Library, 44 Broad St., Westerly
Lecturer Liz Hannan Kading of the Irish Coastal Club will delve into the Irish ancestry of Hallowe’en. For more information, visit westerlylibrary.org or email irishcoastalclub@yahoo.com.
Women and their Wardrobes during the New England Revolution
11 a.m.; North Stonington Historical Society, 1 Wyassup Road, North Stonington
Underpinning the sensationalism of battle reports and broadsides is the often silent steadiness of women’s work with textiles. Choices made about fashion, fabric consumption and creation drove the course of Revolution just as determinedly as any congress. Tickets are $10. For tickets and more information, visit NorthStoningtonHistorical.org
Rodney Crowell with Secret Sisters
8 p.m.; The United, 5 Canal St., Westerly
As part of the Nashville North series of concerts Secret Sisters will open for Rodney Crowell. Tickets are $63.60 and $68.60 at unitedtheatre.org or call 401-388-8208.
Mystic Dead to perform
8 p.m.; The Knickerbocker Music Center, 35 Railroad Ave., Westerly
Advance tickets are $18; $20 at the door. For tickets and more information, visit knickmusic.com.
"Lost Lear" performance
7:30 p.m.; Connecticut College's Athey Center, Palmer Auditorium, 270 Mohegan Ave. Parkway, New London
"Lost Lear," written and directed by Dan Colley, follows the story of a retired actress with dementia. Tickets are $8 to $30. For tickets and more information, visit conncoll.edu/arts-culture/the-arts-at-connecticut-college or call 860-447-1911.
Sunday, Oct. 26
Halloween Parade and Magic Show
Noon-1:45 p.m.; Stonington Borough Fire Dept., 100 Main St., Stonington
The annual parade will begin at noon. At 1 p.m., the Justin Mazz magic show will begin. Ice cream cups will be given to children. For more information, visit facebook.com/StoningtonBoroughFireDepartment.
Sandy Allen of The Hoolios
8 p.m.; The Knickerbocker Music Center, 35 Railroad Ave., Westerly
Free concert in the Tap Room. For more information, visit knickmusic.com.
Monday, Oct. 27
Human Trafficking Red Flags lecture
5:30 p.m.; Groton Public Library, 52 Newtown Road, Groton
Sarah Corella and Nicole Murowsky from the Connecticut Department of Children and Families will focus on human trafficking red flag information. Registration is suggested. To register, call 860-441-6750 or visit the online calendar at grotonpl.org.
Tuesday, Oct. 28
Musical presentation with Noam Makover
6-7:30 p.m.; Westerly Library auditorium, 44 Broad St., Westerly
Westerly Library's artist-in-residence Noam Makover will invite participants to have an open discussion about composition and music production techniques, discipline in music and inspiration. Registration required. To register and for more information, visit westerlylibrary.org or email awagner@westerlylibrary.org.
Moth Night! lecture and potluck
6-8 p.m.; Weeden Farm, 17 Matunuck Beach Road, South Kingstown
South Kingstown Land Trust is hosting a community potluck and a presentation from David Gregg, executive director of the Rhode Island Natural History Survey. A guided walk to observe and identify moths drawn to illuminated sheets will follow. Attendees are asked to bring a dish to share for the potluck. Registration is required. Suggested donation is $10. To register, visit sklt.org or call 401-789-0962.
Wednesday, Oct. 29
All about Bats
6-7 p.m.; Westerly Library auditorium, 44 Broad St., Westerly
Ginny Apple, Master Wildlife Conservationist with the CT DEEP, will discuss the economic value of bats, their migration and hibernation patterns, decline and disease as well as steps the public can take to help ensure the health and safety of our bat populations. Registration is required. To register and for more information, visit westerlylibrary.org, email reference@westerlylibrary.org, or call 401-596-2877, ext. 306.
Literary Salon and Open Mic: Halloween edition
6:30 p.m.; The Gazebo at Wilcox Park, 44 Broad St., Westerly
Jessica P. Wick will host a Halloween edition of the Michael DePaola Literary Salon & Open Mic, featuring a miscellany of mythic and moving works from invited guest readers to a poetry and prose open mic featuring your creativity; musicians are welcome. Ricardo Rebelo, horror writer and filmmaker, will be special guest reader. For more information or to reserve a time slot, visit unitedtheatre.org or call 401-388-8208.
Karaoke night
7 p.m.; Bradford Social Club, 2 Bowling Lane, Bradford
Wednesday night karaoke with Peter Delasanta. Dinner available on site. For more information, visit facebook.com/people/Bradford-Social-Club-RI/61561639483243.
The Sanderson Sisters
6:30 p.m.; The Stonington Free Library, 20 High St., Stonington
The Sanderson Sisters of "Hocus Pocus" fame will lead a family-friendly program for all ages. Registration required. To register, visit stoningtonfreelibrary.org.
"20 Amazing places to Fly Fish in New England that You May Not Have Heard of or Tried"
6 p.m.; Elks Lodge Rhode Island 2285, 42 Nooseneck Hill Road, West Greenwich
Lou Zambello has fly fished all over the world, guided fly fishing in Maine, written four books and numerous magazine articles about fly fishing for trout and salmon, and has taught fly-fishing classes. Non-members are welcome. RSVP at rhodeislandTU.org or call 401-225-7712.
Thursday, Oct. 30
Lecture: Plantation Goods: A Material History of American Slavery
7 p.m.; The Peace Dale Museum of Art and Culture, 1058 Kingstown Road, South Kingstown
Seth Rockman of Brown University will discuss in detail how slavery could not have existed without help from the North and how it affected the nation’s economic growth. The lecture will also be livestreamed on the museum's YouTube channel: youtube.com/@pdmac6899. For more information, visit peacedalemuseum.org/programs/evening-programs.
Oct. 30-Nov. 16
"Keep on Laughing"
Various; The Arctic Playhouse, 1249 Main St., West Warwick
The ladies of "Exit Laughing" are as zany and funny as ever. Tickets are $20. For tickets and more information,visit thearcticplayhouse.com or call 401-573-3443.
